description: Each invoice's cost ratio is its summed product cost ÷ its summed total cost.

c.request: For each invoice in `Invoice_Line_Items`, show the invoice number, the invoice's ratio of product cost (`derived_product_cost`) to total cost (`derived_total_cost`), how many line items it has, and that ratio divided by the average ratio across all invoices. Ignore missing values throughout, and return rows only when that overall average exists. Sort by the relative figure from highest to lowest, with missing values last, show the top 10, and don't round anything. Each invoice's cost ratio is its summed product cost ÷ its summed total cost.
c.sql:
WITH invoice_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    invoice_number,
    SUM(derived_product_cost) as total_product_cost,
    SUM(derived_total_cost) as total_invoice_cost,
    COUNT(*) as line_item_count
  FROM Invoice_Line_Items
  GROUP BY invoice_number
),
invoice_ratios AS (
  SELECT 
    invoice_number,
    line_item_count,
    CASE 
      WHEN total_invoice_cost > 0
        THEN total_product_cost / total_invoice_cost 
      ELSE NULL 
    END as cost_ratio
  FROM invoice_stats
),
average_ratio_calc AS (
  SELECT AVG(cost_ratio) as avg_ratio
  FROM invoice_ratios
),
final_result AS (
  SELECT 
    ir.invoice_number,
    ir.cost_ratio,
    ir.line_item_count,
    ar.avg_ratio,
    CASE 
      WHEN ar.avg_ratio IS NOT NULL AND ir.cost_ratio IS NOT NULL
        THEN ir.cost_ratio / ar.avg_ratio
      ELSE NULL
    END as relative_ratio
  FROM invoice_ratios ir
  CROSS JOIN average_ratio_calc ar
)
SELECT 
  invoice_number,
  cost_ratio,
  line_item_count,
  relative_ratio
FROM final_result
WHERE avg_ratio IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY relative_ratio IS NULL ASC, relative_ratio DESC
LIMIT 10

a.request: For each invoice number in `Invoice_Line_Items`, give the invoice number, the invoice's cost ratio, its number of line items, and its relative ratio. To get the invoice's cost ratio, add up `derived_product_cost` over its lines and divide by the sum of `derived_total_cost` over its lines, ignoring missing values in each sum. The relative ratio is the invoice's cost ratio divided by the average of all invoices' cost ratios (ignoring missing values). Return rows only when that overall average exists. Sort by the relative ratio from highest to lowest, with missing values last, show the top 10, and don't round anything.
a.sql: WITH invoice_stats AS (SELECT invoice_number, SUM(derived_product_cost) as total_product_cost, SUM(derived_total_cost) as total_cost, COUNT(*) as line_item_count FROM Invoice_Line_Items GROUP BY invoice_number), invoice_ratios AS (SELECT invoice_number, CASE WHEN total_cost > 0 THEN total_product_cost / total_cost ELSE NULL END as cost_ratio, line_item_count FROM invoice_stats), average_ratio AS (SELECT AVG(cost_ratio) as avg_ratio FROM invoice_ratios) SELECT ir.invoice_number, ir.cost_ratio, ir.line_item_count, ir.cost_ratio / ar.avg_ratio as relative_ratio FROM invoice_ratios ir CROSS JOIN average_ratio ar WHERE ar.avg_ratio IS NOT NULL ORDER BY relative_ratio IS NULL ASC, relative_ratio DESC LIMIT 10

d.request: For each invoice, calculate the aggregate cost ratio as the sum of derived_product_cost divided by the sum of derived_total_cost across all its line items, count the line items per invoice, compute the mean cost ratio across all invoices, display the invoice number, its cost ratio, line item count, and the cost ratio divided by the mean ratio, exclude rows with null values, sort by the relative ratio descending with nulls last, and return the top 10 rows.
d.sql:
WITH invoice_aggregates AS (
  SELECT
    invoice_number,
    SUM(derived_product_cost) as sum_product_cost,
    SUM(derived_total_cost) as sum_total_cost,
    COUNT(*) as line_item_count
  FROM Invoice_Line_Items
  WHERE derived_product_cost IS NOT NULL 
    AND derived_total_cost IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY invoice_number
),
cost_ratios AS (
  SELECT
    invoice_number,
    line_item_count,
    sum_product_cost / sum_total_cost as cost_ratio
  FROM invoice_aggregates
  WHERE sum_total_cost IS NOT NULL AND sum_total_cost > 0
),
mean_ratio AS (
  SELECT AVG(cost_ratio) as mean_cost_ratio
  FROM cost_ratios
)
SELECT
  cr.invoice_number,
  cr.cost_ratio,
  cr.line_item_count,
  cr.cost_ratio / mr.mean_cost_ratio as relative_ratio
FROM cost_ratios cr
CROSS JOIN mean_ratio mr
ORDER BY cr.cost_ratio / mr.mean_cost_ratio DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10

b.request: For each invoice, show the invoice number, the ratio of the invoice's total derived_product_cost to total derived_total_cost (summed across its line items), the count of its line items, and this ratio divided by the average ratio of all invoices (excluding nulls and returning only when that average exists), sorted by the normalized ratio from highest to lowest with nulls last, limited to the top 10 rows, with no rounding.
b.sql: WITH invoice_ratios AS (SELECT invoice_number, SUM(derived_product_cost) / SUM(derived_total_cost) as ratio, COUNT(*) as line_item_count FROM Invoice_Line_Items GROUP BY invoice_number), average_ratio AS (SELECT AVG(ratio) as avg_ratio FROM invoice_ratios WHERE ratio IS NOT NULL) SELECT ir.invoice_number, ir.ratio, ir.line_item_count, ir.ratio / ar.avg_ratio as normalized_ratio FROM invoice_ratios ir CROSS JOIN average_ratio ar WHERE ar.avg_ratio IS NOT NULL ORDER BY normalized_ratio DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10
